title: What separates 7/7 from 6/7 across all 21 benchmark runs
subtitle: Patterns from 21 published runs, 8 harnesses, and 15 models.
description: A 7-slide meta-synthesis of all 21 published Capy Bench runs: where the 7 partial runs failed (S5 & S7), why duration and turns don't predict success, the Speed × Cost Pareto frontier, and what actually separates 7/7 winners.

slides.lead: **14 runs** cleared every stage; **7 runs** stalled short — and partial runs actually finished slightly faster on average.

slides.label: THE PARETO FRONTIER
slides.headlinePrimary: Four runs define the Speed × Cost frontier.
slides.headlineMuted: From $0.00 free tier to 25-minute flagship speed.

barCompare.label: Speed Among the 4 Frontier Champions (Lower = Faster)

slides.footnote: * Only 3 runs are strictly Pareto-optimal (hy4-flash, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-sol); muse-spark ($0.14) is the cheapest paid 7/7.

slides.label: PATTERN #1 REAL GATEKEEPERS
slides.headlineMuted: Live HTTP (S5) and PTY Ctrl-C (S7) separate the field.

steps.title: S5: synthetic tests hide HTTP bugs (18/21)
steps.desc: Hand-rolled chunked parsers passed local test suites, then broke on live Cloudflare `301` redirects (`glm-5.3-flash Low/Max`, `pi-deepseek`).

steps.title: S7: real terminals break shortcuts (17/21)
steps.desc: Foreground PTY `Ctrl-C` exposed BEAM boot races, `SIGTERM` shutdowns, bare escripts, and sandbox blind spots (`subq-savant`, `muse-code`, `deepseek-flash`).

steps.title: Winners audit runtime internals first
steps.desc: The cleanest 7/7 runs read OTP source (`erl_signal_handler.erl`, `httpc_handler.erl`) instead of guessing through trial-and-error.

callout.title: Why Holdout Probes Matter
callout.body: Every single `<7/7` run reported **green local tests** — only live HTTP and real foreground PTY holdouts caught the bugs.

slides.label: PATTERN #2 HARNESS MULTIPLIER
slides.headlinePrimary: Your harness moves the needle as much as the model.

steps.title: muse-spark-1.3: Pi vs Muse Code
steps.desc: Same weights flipped from **6/7** (`77m`, `$0.25`) on native Muse Code to **7/7** (`56m`, `$0.14`) on third-party Pi.

steps.title: deepseek-flash: Pi → DSH → OMP
steps.desc: Across 3 harnesses, the exact same budget family climbed **4/7 → 5/7 → 6/7** at `$0.13–$0.19`.

steps.title: gemini-4-carbon: AGY vs OMP
steps.desc: Switching from Antigravity CLI to OMP shaved **25 minutes** (`88m → 63m`) and cut cost **-17%** (`$7.16 → $5.91`).

callout.title: Prompt Size, Sandbox & Batching
callout.body: Lean system prompts, real PTY access, and parallel tool batching (`1.86×` on Argon OMP) compound on every single turn.

slides.label: CROSS-BOARD CAVEATS
slides.headlinePrimary: 4 metrics that lie if you read them alone.

items.head: Total tokens without cache rate
items.text: `94%–99.5%` prefix caching cut bills by **80%–95%** — a `73M`-token run can cost `$0.25` or `$6.95` depending on cache-read rates.

items.head: Raw tool error percentage
items.text: Gemini 4 AGY had **100% file-edit accuracy** yet showed `11%–14%` tool errors from deliberate red-phase TDD test runs.

items.head: Green tests without git hygiene
items.text: `erl_crash.dump` files (2.9–5.5 MB) slipped into git history across `hy4-flash`, `glm-5.3-flash`, and `muse-spark` via `git add -A`.

items.head: Single-run variance (n=1)
items.text: Real-world API stalls (`19m57s` on Carbon, `21m` aborts on GLM Low) and temporary free tiers shift individual run numbers.

slides.label: TAKEAWAYS & ARCHIVE
slides.headlinePrimary: 3 rules for picking a coding agent today.

items.head: Pick the tier for your constraint
Don't blindly crank effort to Max
items.text: Middle-high effort (`High`) beat `Max` on completion, speed, and cost — and concise thinking (`17k–25k`) beat bloated loops.

items.head: Audit the harness & holdouts, not just the model
items.text: The best weights fail inside a blind sandbox or bloated prompt — always verify against live targets and real terminals.
